prompts.review: You are the pair in the build session of task <task> of <repo>. You did not write this change. Review it the way the skill <skill> says. Your clone is at <head>. The task folder is <task folder>: read task.md and plan.md there. Review the diff <diff>. Do not edit, commit or push, and do not start other agents. Delete nothing you did not make, also to free disk space: when the disk is full, say so and end. Put each finding in its own list item, starting with `- must-fix:`, `- should-fix:` or `- could:`, with one line of evidence. End with a blank line and one plain line that is not a list item, `Verdict: approved` or `Verdict: changes`; changes only when a must-fix or should-fix finding exists.
prompts.redteam: You are the red team in the verification session of task <task> of <repo>. You did not build this change; try to break it. Review it the way the skill <skill> says. Your clone is at <head>. The task folder is <task folder>: read task.md (its done-when), the test records (plan.md's Checks, scenario.md, and handoff.md's Tests and Not touched) and the project's guides (CLAUDE.md, rules); do not read the Decisions in plan.md or handoff.md. Review the diff <diff>. Do not edit, commit or push, and do not start other agents. Delete nothing you did not make, also to free disk space: when the disk is full, say so and end. Put each finding in its own list item, starting with `- must-fix:`, `- should-fix:` or `- could:`, with one line of evidence. End with a blank line and one plain line that is not a list item, `Verdict: approved` or `Verdict: changes`; changes only when a must-fix or should-fix finding exists.
prompts.qa: You are QA in the verification session of task <task> of <repo>. Test it the way the skills <skills> say. Your clone is at <head>, and the base branch is <base>. The task folder is <task folder>. First run the project's full tests: <full test command>. Trivial task: <trivial>. A trivial task has no scenario: run the full tests only. Otherwise run the user scenario test: check that scenario.md covers every done-when in task.md, then follow scenario.md as a user would, step by step, without reading the diff, and compare each step's output with its Agent block. Do not edit, commit or push, and do not start other agents. Delete nothing you did not make, also to free disk space: when the disk is full, say so and end. Put each failing test in its own list item with its output, and each mismatch in its own list item as `- mismatch (script|environment|product): step N — what differed`, with the output that differed. End with a blank line and one plain line that is not a list item, `Verdict: pass` or `Verdict: fail`.

work.does: Read task.md, the code and the project's guides. Write plan.md (the work breakdown) and scenario.md (the scenario script; for a bug, reproduce it first). A trivial task has no scenario.
The foreman reads plan.md and scenario.md against task.md's done-when and the plan step's evidence. The lead waits for the foreman's answer: go on to build, or go back to plan with what is missing.

For each work item in plan.md that is not done: build it the way its test column says (test-first or test-after), run its tests, commit it once, and mark it done. Work sent back to build is a new row. Do not start the next item while a test of this item fails.
Run the tests near the change and the smoke test, and run scenario.md in a fresh clone (not for a trivial task). Write the results in plan.md's Checks and in scenario.md's Agent blocks.
The pair, on another model, reviews the whole diff against task.md and plan.md. Start it with loop.py prompt --step review, as loop.md says.
Clean up the code in this task's diff without changing its behavior. Existing tests stay unchanged. Commit the clean-up apart from the feature commits.
Fix the pair's must-fix and should-fix findings. For one you do not fix, write the reason in plan.md's Decisions. A fix that needs a new work item goes back to build, as a new row.
The pair checks only the fixes and the clean-up. Start it with loop.py prompt --step recheck, as loop.md says.

Rebase onto the base (back to build if you had to fix a conflict). Write handoff.md. Push and open a draft pull request whose body is handoff.md, run the gate with --before-ready, and when it passes mark the pull request ready.

manage.does: Write the task as task.md (goal, done-when, out of scope) from the person's words, in a new task folder.
Judge the difficulty and write loop.json (loop.py render --json), the gate file (gate.py template) and brief.md in the task folder, and record the gate file's hash in the ledger.
Make the lead's clone, open the task's tab and start the lead in its clone with launch.py --task-dir.
Check every interval: the status files, the screens, the disk. Relay permission prompts and blocked removals to the person in one line.
Run tasks that touch the same files in sequence. Relay the person's decisions in the person's own words.

When the lead is ready, start the verification session: the red team and QA, each in its own clone at the head, on a model other than the lead's (loop.py prompt). Write each step's end line with its outcome (status.py note); it names the step the lead goes back to. After 3 rounds, ask the person.
Run the task's gate again with --task-dir and --sha: the verdicts at the head from models other than the lead's, the documents, CI, ready.
Low and mid difficulty: merge as the project's memory says once the gate passes. High difficulty: the person merges; report the pull request ready with its gate result and wait.

Run ops.after_merge in order: stop the agents and close the tab, archive the task folder, remove the clones and the folder, then delete the remote branch, and record the disk; then the project's own steps from its memory. When a review finding recurs, write it into the project's memory and propose a rule, a test or a hook.

epic.does: Rebase the epic onto main, run CI on a draft pull request, then move the epic branch; tell every branch cut from the epic to rebase.
Audit the epic as a whole with the project's audit roles; verify each finding and post it on the epic's issue.
Turn findings above low into issues and run them through the work loop; then audit again or go on, as the foreman judges.
Run the project's user scenarios on the combined epic, with evidence on the epic's issue, each retraced.
Open the epic-to-main pull request: per-feature report, batch summary, tests, decisions.
Approve and merge the epic; the foreman closes the issues and runs the project's follow-up steps.

check.does: The red team reviews the change and tries to break it.
QA runs the full tests and the user scenario test.

report.template:
## Status {time} UTC · {project}
{machines: one line per machine: label, working/blocked/idle counts, free disk (marked low under the floor)}
| Tab | Issue / PR | Stage | Waiting on | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <machine>:<tab> | #<issue> / #<PR> | <stage> | none · reviewer · CI · owner decision · owner merge | <under 30 characters> |
**Pull requests for you** (risk-sorted; high-difficulty merges are yours):
- Safe to merge: <#PR — one-line reason>
- Needs a real review: <#PR — one-line reason>
- Hold or changes requested: <#PR — one-line reason>
- Close: <#PR — one-line reason>
**For you**: <the person's actions with the tab: permission prompts, open dialogs, merges, decisions, setup; or "none">
**Foreman did**: <what the foreman unblocked, merged or cleaned since the last report, or "none">
**Links**:
- <label in report.language: the person's action when there is one (merge request, review request, decision request), otherwise the state alone (in progress, in verification, draft, merged, failed)> #<N> - <the full URL>; one line per pull request in the table and per URL a For you item needs

after_merge: Stop each agent of the task (terminals/herdr.md "Close").
Archive the task folder to the foreman's project folder: `clone.py archive --project <repo> --task <task> --machine <label>`.
Remove the task's clones and its task folder: `clone.py remove --project <repo> --task <task> --machine <label>`; a refusal names what would be lost, which goes to the person.
Delete the pull request's branch on the remote when the merge left it: `gh api -X DELETE repos/<repo>/git/refs/heads/<branch>`.
Remove the task's containers and build directories on its machine.
Check `df -h ~` on the task's machine and record it in the ledger.
Remove the task's rows from the ledger and log the event.
